rationale: The primary DASS depression improvement was 2.37 points larger with 28 mg/day extract (95% CI 0.23 to 4.51), and 21/43 versus 11/43 met the 7-point improvement threshold. The prospective registration excludes Parkinson disease. This is an industry-funded extract trial.

Narrative synthesis separates stigma, petal and constituent preparations, with no formal risk-of-bias tool. It reports favorable results in earlier non-Parkinson depression trials and no independent cohort. The review search ends before the matched whole-powder Parkinson trial.

The registered secondary PROMIS Sleep Disturbance contrast is 0.38 points (95% CI −2.40 to 3.16). The separate sleep-related impairment contrast favors extract by 2.99 (95% CI 0.12 to 5.86) without multiplicity adjustment. The registry excludes Parkinson disease and has no dedicated insomnia severity scale.

Secondary PROMIS Sleep-Related Impairment T-score improved by 2.99 points relative to placebo (95% CI 0.12 to 5.86). Its composite includes tiredness and the study reports no isolated fatigue result. Ground culinary exposure and Parkinson disease differ from the registered study.

A public Dakota and Ojibwe food resource records sun-drying cranberries and use of dried berries. It supplies species and preparation context with no depression, diagnosed Parkinson population or efficacy finding.
